summary: We developed CHRONO TERRA, a 100% real-world, high-performance web platform deployed live on Cloudflare Pages that empowers users to investigate multi-decade climate trends across the Atlantic Ocean. Built with pure HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, the platform connects directly to live NASA POWER (MERRA-2) APIs and includes robust offline fallbacks to guarantee uninterrupted operation during evaluation.   The application features an interactive 3D Atlantic Globe and synchronized 2D map, allowing researchers and citizens to inspect critical regional hotspots such as Hurricane Alley and the Subpolar Cold Blob. To directly address the "Earth-System-Trend-Detective" challenge, CHRONO TERRA incorporates an in-browser statistical analysis engine that performs Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, Mann-Kendall non-parametric trend tests, and seasonal de-trending (anomaly mode) to isolate true climate signals from cyclic seasonal weather swings.   CHRONO TERRA is vital because it transforms complex climate telemetries into an intuitive NASA Mission Control interface, making it seamless to distinguish genuine, statistically significant climate trends from random natural variability.
details:
Here is the complete, polished project response formatted with clean headings

Project Details

  • Project Title: CHRONO TERRA
  • Team Name: STARK HELIX
  • Developer: SURAFEL GASHAW
  • Live Deployed URL: https://chrono-terra.pages.dev/

1. What does it do and how does it work?

CHRONO TERRA is an interactive, web-based climate investigation platform designed to explore multi-decade environmental trends across the Atlantic Ocean.

  • How it works: The platform connects directly to the NASA POWER (MERRA-2) API to fetch real-world monthly time-series data for parameters like surface temperature, precipitation, and wind speed.
  • The Workflow: Users can click anywhere on an interactive 3D Atlantic Globe or choose pre-set regional hotspots (such as Hurricane Alley or the Subpolar Cold Blob). The app then strips away seasonal cycles (computing anomalies) and runs an in-browser statistical analysis engine to calculate Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, Mann-Kendall trend tests, and effective sample size corrections.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Instant Accessibility: Runs 100% in the browser with zero installation, backend servers, or complex build setups required.
  • Scientific Rigor: Unlike basic charts that can be skewed by winter-to-summer swings, it automatically de-seasons data and calculates true statistical significance (p-values and confidence intervals).
  • Offline Reliability: Features robust caching and pre-built baseline datasets, ensuring it functions seamlessly even during live judging with limited or no internet connectivity.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The goal of CHRONO TERRA is to democratize climate data analysis. It bridges the gap between complex NASA satellite/reanalysis records and public understanding. By translating abstract telemetries into a clear NASA Mission Control-style dashboard with intuitive significance gauges, it empowers students, educators, and citizen scientists to distinguish genuine, long-term climate signals from random natural variability.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend & UI: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), and Chart.js for responsive time-series visualizations.
  • 3D Globe Visualization: Globe.gl / Three.js for the interactive 3D Atlantic Ocean model.
  • Data & Statistics: NASA Langley POWER Project (MERRA-2 reanalysis API), custom JavaScript statistical engine for OLS regression and Mann-Kendall testing.
  • Deployment Platform: Cloudflare Pages for high-speed, global edge hosting(https://chrono-terra.pages.dev/)).

5. How is your project creative?

CHRONO TERRA breaks away from static, dull scientific reports by turning climate exploration into an interactive detective game. Users can compare two distinct Atlantic regions side-by-side on the 3D globe with opposite trend comparison arcs, toggle a "Marine Heatwave" case-study mode, and instantly see a statistical verdict gauge that acts as a "coincidence meter" for climate anomalies.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Statistical Validity: We factored in serial autocorrelation (neighboring months being similar) by incorporating effective sample size adjustments ($n_{eff}$) so that trend significance isn't falsely over-optimistic.
  • Performance & Speed: Built as a lightweight, single-page application that optimizes memory usage and leverages GPU-accelerated rendering for the 3D globe.
  • User Experience (UX): Designed with dual Clean Scientific Light and Obsidian Dark modes, mobile responsiveness, and an intuitive 3-step detective wizard for beginners.
